questions.title: Definition of agenesis
questions.question: Complete absence of an organ is called

explanations.A: Incorrect. Dysplasia is disordered growth with loss of uniformity of individual cells and their architectural orientation, a pattern seen within a tissue that still exists -- not the complete failure of an organ to form.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Anaplasia is loss of cellular differentiation, a feature of malignant tumour cells reverting to a more primitive state -- it describes a cell's degree of differentiation, not the complete absence of an organ.
explanations.C: Correct. Agenesis is the complete congenital failure of an organ to form during development, so the organ is entirely absent at birth. It is a developmental anomaly, distinct from the four adaptive cellular responses (hypertrophy, hyperplasia, atrophy, metaplasia) that an already-formed tissue can undergo.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hyperplasia is an increase in the number of cells of an organ that has already formed -- the opposite situation from an organ that never formed at all.

questions.learning_objective: Define agenesis as the complete congenital absence of an organ, distinguishing it from dysplasia, anaplasia and hyperplasia.
